editorial.headline: Fuel Wholesale Is Nationally Open, but Bali Turns on Risk Scope
editorial.standfirst: This wholesale activity spans conventional, renewable and low-carbon fuels, with full national foreign ownership but a scope-sensitive PMA route in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is the wholesale trade of fuels and closely related products: fossil fuels alongside lower-carbon or carbon-free alternatives, as well as grease, lubricants and oils. Its commercial range is unusually broad, taking in crude petroleum, diesel, gasoline, fuel oil, kerosene and solar; biofuels, recycled-carbon fuels and synthetic fuels; charcoal, coal, coke, firewood, wood pellets, biomass and naphtha. It also includes LPG, LNG, butane, propane and their related bio or renewable forms, whether blended or pure, plus nuclear fuel. Hydrogen sits outside the group’s stated boundary.

The code is open to businesses at every listed scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. In practical terms, it is for an enterprise whose activity is wholesale distribution across that fuel-and-related-products universe, rather than a narrow label for one commodity alone. The breadth matters because the record describes distinct fuel forms, product families and energy sources within a single wholesale activity. A founder should therefore match the registered activity to the precise business scope being undertaken, especially where the product mix reaches beyond conventional petroleum fuels.

At the national level, the PMA position is straightforward: the activity is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That is a full national foreign-ownership position, supported in the record by Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali, however, is not a simple extension of that national reading. The province permanently blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the island. For this activity, the Bali result is scope-dependent rather than categorically blocked: at the Besar scale, OSS risk is low for some scopes and higher for others.

That distinction is the operative one for a foreign-owned business considering Bali. The record says PMA registration in Bali is available only by declaring the higher-risk scope, and it directs verification in live OSS for the exact activity. National openness therefore remains real, but it does not itself settle the Bali registration outcome. The relevant question is not whether fuel wholesale is nationally open—it is—but whether the particular activity scope declared in Bali falls on the registrable side of the province’s risk-based rule.
editorial.pullQuote: A 100% national foreign-ownership ceiling does not by itself settle the Bali registration outcome.
